Extend the reconnect-lifecycle REGISTRIES table with a WHERE-THE-DISCONNECT-LANDS axis driven off FakeSynapse.onRequest / holdMessages — {during /directory lookup, during /join, during the positioning /sync, during /messages} x {fetchRecent, post, subscribe} — asserting all four registries are empty after the sequence AND that no request is issued after teardown. The current lifecycles only disconnect at coarse points (after subscribe, racing an in-flight subscribe), so no row can land inside the join.

summary: `revertToProvisionalNick()` mutates the connection-wide `this.nick` but neither records the old nick in `roomNicks` for rooms already entered under it, nor forgets/re-joins them (the way `switchNick` does). Every subsequent `post` to those rooms fails the `resourceOf(from) === this.occupantNick(room)` provenance check in `onGroupchat`, so its reflection is dropped and the post stalls to POST_TIMEOUT_MS — permanently, because nothing ever re-reconciles the nick.
failure: Live against Prosody (throwaway container, examples/dev-compose image/flags): a second account pins nick `alice` in room B. Plugin connects with no `backend_config.nick`; `post(A,'alice','first')` -> ok (`joined[A]` under nick `alice`); `post(B,'alice','second')` -> join answered `conflict`, plugin reverts `this.nick` to `parley-<rand>` and joins B -> ok; `post(A,'alice','third')` -> `ERR post reflection timeout in qa-1-klj8ul@muc.parley.local` after 15905 ms, and every later post to A does the same. This is exactly the stall the `roomNicks` JSDoc says the per-room map exists to prevent — the map is only ever written on a service rewrite (status 210), never on the plugin's own revert.
remediation: Make every mutation of `this.nick` reconcile existing occupancy. Either (a) in `revertToProvisionalNick`, before assigning, `for (const room of this.joined.keys()) this.roomNicks.set(room, oldNick)` so those rooms keep recognising their own reflections, or (b) route the revert through `switchNick`-style handling: `forgetAllRooms()` + re-drive `ensureJoinedRoom` for each, so every room is actually re-entered under the new nick. Option (b) also keeps `parley_list_users` attribution consistent across rooms.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS "a connection-wide occupant-nick change leaves a previously joined room addressed under the stale nick". Parameterize `join-recovery.test.ts` over a *room count* axis (>=2 rooms) crossed with each nick-changing event (`conflict` revert, `switchNick` on first-post identity adoption, service rewrite status 210, reconnect re-join) and assert, for EVERY room joined before the event, that a subsequent `post` resolves within a bound well under POST_TIMEOUT_MS. The existing table is single-room only, so no row can observe cross-room divergence.

summary: `FakeXmpp` holds a single `nick` field for the whole connection: `answerJoin` overwrites it on every join and `onPost` reflects from `${room}/${this.nick}` for all rooms. The fixture therefore cannot represent one connection occupying room A as `alice` and room B as `parley-xxx` — which is precisely the state `XmppPlugin.roomNicks` exists to model and precisely the state the confirmed nick-revert defect creates. Every fake-driven test agrees with the plugin by construction.
failure: The same scenario as the confirmed defect, written against `FakeXmpp` (post A as alice; conflictNicks.add('alice'); post B; post A again), PASSES — `third post -> arch-3 after 0 ms` — because the fake reflects room A's message from the connection's *current* nick. The identical scenario against real Prosody fails with a 15.9 s reflection timeout. A fixture that agrees with the bug is counted as coverage for the branch it hides.
remediation: Give `FakeXmpp` per-room occupancy state: `occupantNick: Map<room, nick>` written by `answerJoin` from the presence's own resource, read by `onPost` and `endOccupancy` when composing `from`. Then `nick` becomes a per-room query rather than a connection-wide field, and `attach()` seeds the map for the room it pre-joins.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS "a stand-in whose state is coarser than the production state it models". Add a fixture-fidelity case that joins two rooms under two different nicks and asserts the fake reflects each room from its own nick; then reuse it as the substrate for a parameterized per-room-nick table (reflection provenance, occupancy-loss attribution, 210 rewrite in one room only). The existing `join-attribution.test.ts` drives one room and so cannot fail on this.

summary: `isPlaintextRemote` classifies any host matching `/^127\./` as loopback. That regex is unanchored at the end, so a *hostname* that merely begins with `127.` is treated as loopback and the cleartext-SASL-PLAIN warning — the only guard on this path — is suppressed.
failure: `isPlaintextRemote('xmpp://127.evil.com:5222')` returns `false` (verified by executing the exported function). Result: `connect({ service: 'xmpp://127.evil.com:5222', password: 's3cret' })` emits no `SECURITY: ... plaintext scheme to a non-loopback host` warning, and `@xmpp/client` then offers SASL PLAIN over an opportunistically-upgraded stream to a remote attacker-controlled host. `ws://127.attacker.net` behaves the same.
remediation: Match the IPv4 loopback block as an address, not as a string prefix: require the host to parse as four dot-separated decimal octets with the first equal to 127 (e.g. `/^127(\.\d{1,3}){3}$/`, plus the existing `localhost` / `::1` cases). Anything that is not a literal IP or the exact string `localhost` is remote.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS "a loopback/private-range check that matches a prefix of a hostname rather than an address". Extend the `LOOPBACK`/`REMOTE` table in `creds-warning.test.ts` with an adversarial-lookalike row set that must all classify REMOTE: `127.evil.com`, `127.0.0.1.evil.com`, `localhost.evil.com`, `::1.evil.com`, `0177.0.0.1`, `2130706433` — and keep the genuine `127.0.0.44`/`[::1]` rows as the negative control. A generator that appends `.evil.example` to every LOOPBACK entry and asserts the transport warning fires covers inputs nobody enumerated.

summary: `adoptIdentityNick` memoizes on the FIRST identity it ever sees (`this.nickAdoption ??= this.switchNick(nickFor(identity))`). Every later `post` with a different `identity` is attributed to the first handle, with no error and no diagnostic — the seam's per-call `identity` parameter silently stops meaning anything after call one.
failure: `post(t, asHandle('alice'), 'x')` then `post(t, asHandle('bob'), 'y')`: `nickFor('bob')` is never evaluated, the join presence is never re-driven, and the archived sender of both messages is `alice`. `fetchRecent` therefore returns `senderHandle: 'alice'` for a message the caller posted as `bob`, and `parley_list_users` never learns `bob` exists.
remediation: Fail fast rather than silently rebind: if `nickFor(identity)` differs from the adopted nick, either drive a nick change for it (as `switchNick` already can) or reject the post with an error naming both handles and pointing at `backend_config.nick` / one-bridge-per-handle. A no-op that changes the message's attribution is the worst of the three options.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS "a seam argument that is honoured on the first call and silently discarded thereafter". Add a parameterized case per seam method that takes a caller-supplied identity/topic-scoped argument, driving two calls with DIFFERENT argument values and asserting the second is either honoured or refused — never accepted-and-ignored. For XMPP the row is `post(t,'alice')` then `post(t,'bob')`, asserting the second message reads back with `senderHandle === 'bob'` or the call rejects.

summary: `revertToProvisionalNick(): boolean` is documented as "Returns whether the nick actually changed", but its only caller (`doJoin`) discards the value and re-derives the answer from `this.nick !== usedNick`. The two conditions are not equivalent (they differ exactly in the concurrent-revert case), so the JSDoc describes a contract nothing consumes and a reader must diff the two predicates to learn which one is authoritative.
failure: Reading `doJoin`, the `conflict` branch is `this.revertToProvisionalNick(); if (this.nick !== usedNick) { ... }` — the returned boolean is dropped on the floor while the JSDoc asserts it is the signal. A maintainer who "simplifies" to `if (this.revertToProvisionalNick())` silently removes the concurrent-revert retry the class comment says is deliberate.
remediation: Make the function `void` and delete the sentence, or have it return the fact the caller actually needs (`nickChangedSince(usedNick)`) and use it. One predicate, one place.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS "a helper whose documented return contract has no consumer" mechanically rather than by review: extend the existing `source-hygiene` style check in `packages/bridge-core/src/source-hygiene.test.ts` to flag private methods with a non-`void` return type whose every call site is an expression statement.

summary: readRecent sizes the since-less window from the STREAM-wide `last_seq`, only falling back to the per-subject `last_by_subj` tail when `num_deleted > 0`. When the topic's stream captures more subjects than the topic's own — a configuration `ensureStream`/`captures()` explicitly accepts — the window is anchored on a foreign publisher's sequence, the widening budget (32 x limit) is exhausted, and the page comes back empty with a cursor far above the topic's real history.
failure: Live NATS 2.10: stream `PW_deploys` created out-of-band with subjects ['pw.>']; plugin configured subject_prefix 'pw.' / stream_prefix 'PW_'; post 'a','b','c' to topic `deploys` (seqs 1-3); then 5000 messages published by anyone to `pw.junk`. `plugin.fetchRecent({topic: deploys})` -> `{messages: [], nextCursor: '1803'}` after 1.2s of wasted pulls. Replaying that cursor as `since` returns `[]` forever: 'a','b','c' are durably stored and permanently unreachable. num_deleted is 0 throughout, so the per-subject `tailSequence()` anchor that would have fixed it never runs.
remediation: Drop the `num_deleted > 0` gate and anchor the window on `streams.getMessage(stream, {last_by_subj: subject})` unconditionally (one extra round trip per since-less read), and/or keep widening while `read.length === 0` until `startSeq <= firstSeq` instead of stopping at WIDEN_ATTEMPTS. Additionally consider refusing, at ensureStream, a pre-existing stream whose subject list is not exactly this topic's subject — every sequence field the plugin reads is then per-topic by construction.
testUpgrade: Widen the fake-JetStream generator behind window.test.ts so a shape can carry FOREIGN sequences: records the pull's filter_subject does not match, but which still count toward `state.messages`/`first_seq`/`last_seq` and leave `num_deleted` at 0. Cross that axis (foreign-tail depth 0, 1, limit, 32*limit, 100*limit) with the existing shapes x positions table, asserting the exact `owed()` page — the class is 'any stream-level counter used where a per-subject one is required', so the same rows also catch a future `first_seq`/`messages` misuse. window.test.ts today cannot see this: every shape's records are all on the topic's own subject, so stream-wide and per-subject state coincide in every row.

summary: `confirmSequence`'s payload-equality check — the half that catches a re-provisioned stream which ALREADY HOLDS a different message at the acked sequence — is vacuous coverage. Deleting the line leaves the whole suite green. Only the 'sequence holds nothing' arm (`isMessageMissing`) is graded, and that is the arm a real re-provision least often presents.
failure: Mutation: delete `if (dec.decode(stored.data) !== payload) throw ackIncarnationUnknown(stream, seq);`. `npx vitest run packages/bridge-nats/test/msg-id.test.ts packages/bridge-nats/test/cursor.test.ts` -> 29 passed, 0 failed. The uncovered real behaviour: stream re-provisioned around a publish, new incarnation already at seq 3 with its own message; `post` returns `<newIncarnation>-3` for a message that landed in the OLD incarnation, which is exactly the id the new incarnation's seq-3 message will mint — core's SeenSet then drops a genuinely new message. Both ackAmbiguities rows in msg-id.test.ts wipe `records`, so getMessage always 404s and the equality branch is never reached.
remediation: No source change needed for the guard itself; add the missing arm to the test table so the guard cannot be deleted silently.
testUpgrade: Parameterize msg-id.test.ts's `ackAmbiguities` over WHAT the surviving incarnation holds at the acked sequence, not just over how the swap is observed: {no message}, {a different message at the same seq}, {a different message at a lower seq and nothing at the acked seq}, {the same content posted by someone else}. Add a fake knob `replaceRecordsWith` so the swapped incarnation can be pre-populated. The class is 'a two-armed guard whose test table only ever exercises one arm' — same row generator should be reused for isStreamMissing/isMessageMissing classification.

summary: The subscribe rebuild's incarnation reset (`if (info.created !== created) { created = info.created; lastSeq = 0; }`) is unexercised. Deleting it keeps the whole fake-backed suite green, and the neighbouring `if (lastSeq > info.state.last_seq)` clamp masks it in every case the tests do construct — but not in the case that matters.
failure: Mutation: delete the `info.created !== created` block. `npx vitest run packages/bridge-nats/test/msg-id.test.ts packages/bridge-nats/test/subscribe-loop.test.ts packages/bridge-nats/test/recovery.test.ts` -> 36 passed, 0 failed. Traced consequence the mutation exposes: live subscription at lastSeq=5; stream deleted and re-created out-of-band; 10 messages land in the new incarnation before the rebuild, so `info.state.last_seq` is 10 and the downward clamp does not fire; the rebuilt consumer starts at opt_start_seq 6 and the new incarnation's messages 1-5 are never delivered on the live path. No test in the package ever re-provisions a stream underneath a live subscribe.

summary: README states `post` reads the incarnation stamp back after its ack so that a stream re-provisioned between two posts "CANNOT re-mint the previous incarnation's ids". `observeIncarnation` swallows every failure by design (its own JSDoc says "the cached incarnation is the best available"), and on that path `post` does exactly what the README says cannot happen.
failure: Trace: stream re-provisioned after the publish ack; `observeIncarnation`'s `streams.info` fails (link blip, auth, timeout) and is swallowed at index.ts:221. `this.incarnations.get(stream)` still holds the OLD token, so `published === incarnations.get(stream)` and `confirmSequence` is skipped entirely. `post` returns `<oldIncarnation>-<seq>` for a message that landed in the new incarnation — and since sequences restart at 1, the old incarnation very likely already handed out that exact id for a different message, so core's SeenSet drops the new one. The README promises this is impossible.
remediation: Either make the failure honest in code — on an `observeIncarnation` failure, mark the stream's incarnation UNKNOWN (or force `confirmSequence`) rather than reusing the last-known token — or soften the README to state the residual window: an incarnation read that fails leaves the id labelled with the last observed incarnation.
testUpgrade: Add a fake knob `infoFailures: n` and a row to msg-id.test.ts's observation table: 'the post-ack incarnation read itself fails'. Assert the same SeenSet property the other rows assert (no id minted after the swap collides with one minted before). The class is 'a doc claim resting on a code path that swallows its own failure' — a docs.test.ts style check listing README's absolute modal claims ('cannot', 'never', 'always') and requiring a named test per claim generalizes it.

summary: `fetchRecent`'s long-poll deadline (`Date.now() + blockMs`) is computed INSIDE `readRecent`, which `withStream` may run a second time. A stream that vanishes mid-poll therefore serves the caller up to 2 x `blockMs`, breaking the bound core states for `catchup.block_max_ms` ("sized under client tool timeouts so a blocked call never trips them").
failure: Trace: `fetchRecent({topic, since, blockMs: 60000})` -> `withStream` -> `readRecent` sets deadline T+60s -> `blockingFetch` -> `jsm.consumers.add` (outside blockingFetch's try, index.ts:384) rejects with 'stream not found' after e.g. 55s because the stream was removed out-of-band -> `isStreamMissing` -> `withStream` re-ensures and re-invokes `readRecent`, which computes a FRESH T'+60s deadline. The MCP `fetch_recent` call blocks ~115s against a stated 60s ceiling; core's `fetchRecentBlocking` awaits the plugin call in full and cannot cut it short without an AbortSignal.
remediation: Compute the deadline in `fetchRecent` (before `withStream`) and pass it down, so a retry inherits the caller's original budget rather than minting a new one; return the empty page with the fallback cursor if the retry starts past the deadline.
testUpgrade: Parameterize a bounded-budget table over every path that can retry or re-enter a caller-supplied wait: {stream missing during consumers.add, during consumers.get, during the iterate} x blockMs in {150, 300, 1000, 5000}, asserting total elapsed < blockMs + slack for each. long-poll.test.ts today pins the upper bound only on the happy path, so any retry wrapper reintroduces the overshoot invisibly; the class is 'a deadline recomputed inside a retried closure'.

summary: subscribe() seeds its delivery watermark from a limit-1 since-less read; that read can come back EMPTY while history exists, because the backward pagination walk terminates on an unusable edge record. lastDeliveredId then falls to 0 and the armed gap-fill replays the ENTIRE topic history through the live handler.
failure: Topic has messages h0,h1,h2. A record with `id: 0` (or `id: -1`) is then appended by anything other than the plugin (`fake.injectRaw({topic, fields:{id:0}})` models the shape the package itself declares reachable — a proxy/older server/hostile realm member). `subscribe(topic, h)` → h receives ['h0','h1','h2'] within 500ms. Reproduced: `tail probe` returns [] because zulipToMessage drops id<=0 and pageAnchor('newest'→'0') then finds nothing older; needsGapFillFrom = 0; gapFill(cursor '0') re-reads and delivers all history as live push. Violates the frozen conformance clause 'subscribe delivers exactly the post-subscribe tail' — the defect the suite says 'has already bitten a shipped backend'.
remediation: Do not derive the watermark from the usable-message projection. Have the tail probe report the highest RAW `id` the server showed (the same raw-vs-usable distinction fetchMessages already applies to termination and to the next anchor), and only treat 0 as the watermark when the server showed no record at all. Equivalently: make fetchMessages expose `sawRawRecords`/`maxRawId` and have subscribe seed from that.
testUpgrade: Parameterize the existing `subscribe delivers exactly the post-subscribe tail` clause over a table of pre-subscribe history states crossed with an unusable NEWEST record: id ∈ {0, -1, 1.5, 1e18, NaN, 'nope', missing} × history length ∈ {0, 1, 3, GAP_FILL_PAGE+1}. Assert the handler receives ONLY post-subscribe messages in every cell. The existing 'replays what is behind a full page of unusable records in the dead window' case only walks the FORWARD gap-fill direction and cannot reach the backward tail probe; the untrusted-payload `limit` table only grades fetchRecent, never the subscribe watermark.

summary: A single 429 on the blocking-fetch wait path (register or the /events long-poll) makes fetchRecent overrun its blockMs by the server's whole Retry-After hint. fetchWithRetry's 429 backoff (net-util sleepUnlessStopped) races only isStopped(), never `init.signal`, so the plugin's deadlineAbort fires into a void.
failure: `plugin.fetchRecent({topic, since: tail, blockMs: 300})` with `fake.rateLimit('GET /api/v1/events', {times:1, headerSeconds:8})` returns after 8018ms (measured); same shape on 'POST /api/v1/register' returns after 8012ms. Because pollForWake raises deadlineMs to blockMs + DEFAULT_DEADLINE_MS, any hint up to ~30s is honoured in full — so a routine Zulip rate limit turns a 300ms-budget fetch_recent into a ~30s one and blows the MCP client tool timeout DESIGN §11 sizes catchup.block_max_ms under.
remediation: Make net-util's 429 backoff race `init.signal` (abort → throw, same as an in-flight abort), so a caller-supplied deadline signal bounds the whole call and not just the bytes in flight. Belt-and-braces in the plugin: race `wake.waited` and the post-wait fetchMessages against an interruptibleDelay to `deadline` in blockingFetch, so no single HTTP call can spend more than the caller's budget.
testUpgrade: Add a 429 row family to the existing `zulip blocking fetchRecent never overruns its blockMs` table: cross the SLOW_STATES dimension with `rateLimit(route, {times:1, headerSeconds: 8})` for EVERY route the wait path touches ('POST /api/v1/register', 'GET /api/v1/events', 'GET /api/v1/messages'), at blockMs ∈ {200, 600, 2000}, asserting elapsed <= blockMs + slack. The current table only models hangs, 500s and holdResponse — none of which reach the retry loop's own sleep — and rate-limit.test.ts only ever 429s 'POST /api/v1/messages', which has no caller budget to overrun.

summary: When no healthy subscribe loop exists, every pass of blockingFetch mints and drops a dedicated event queue at a FLAT 400ms pace (BLOCKED_FETCH_RETRY_MS) with no escalation — unlike the push loop, which backs off to 5s. One blocked fetch against a degraded server issues hundreds of register/poll/delete round trips.
failure: `fetchRecent({topic, since: tail, blockMs: 6000})` with /events answering 400 BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID: measured 15 POST /api/v1/register + 15 DELETE /api/v1/events + 15 GET /api/v1/events in 6s. At core's default catchup.block_max_ms of 60000 that is ~150 registrations and ~450 requests from a SINGLE parley_fetch_recent — past Zulip's default 200 req/min per-user API rate limit, so the call rate-limits the bot by itself and then lands in the 429 stall above.
remediation: Escalate the blocked-fetch pause the way the push loop does (LOOP_BACKOFF_MIN_MS→LOOP_BACKOFF_MAX_MS on consecutive failed wake attempts), and/or reuse one dedicated queue across passes of the same blockingFetch instead of re-registering per pass when the previous registration is still valid.
testUpgrade: Widen `does not spin when the server rejects every event queue it is handed` from one 1200ms/<10 point into a table over blockMs ∈ {1200, 6000, 20000} × degradation mode ∈ {BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID, 500 on /events, 200-with-no-events, /events black hole}, asserting requests-per-second on every loop route stays under a named budget (e.g. registers <= 2 + blockMs/2000). Pinning a raw count at one short duration certifies a pace that is fine for 1.2s and 25x over budget for 60s.

summary: pageAnchor's anti-spin guard — the clause its own comment says to 'keep, so that a server answering with an unmoving id cannot spin the read on one page forever' — is graded by nothing. Deleting it leaves the entire zulip suite green.
failure: Mutation: removed `const current = Number(from); if (Number.isFinite(current) && (backwards ? id >= current : id <= current)) return undefined;` from pageAnchor. `npx vitest run packages/bridge-zulip` → 18 files passed, 358 passed / 1 skipped. The fake never returns a page whose edge record fails to move the anchor (it always excludes the anchor and filters strictly by id), so no fixture can discriminate the guard's presence. A defensive clause counted as coverage that cannot fail is worse than none — and the same shape is what the head commit ('give every clause a negative control') was closing elsewhere.
remediation: Give the fake a lever that models an anchor-violating server (`stallAnchor(route)`: answer a full page whose edge record repeats the requested anchor id, or whose records are all unusable with a non-advancing edge), and assert fetchMessages terminates rather than spinning.
testUpgrade: Parameterize a 'pagination always terminates' case over server-misbehaviour rows: {edge record repeats the anchor, edge record moves backwards, whole page unusable with a non-advancing edge, edge id absent} × direction {since-less backward walk, since-based forward walk} × limit {1, MAX_MESSAGES_PER_FETCH+1}. Each row asserts the call resolves inside a bound AND that fake.requestCount('GET /api/v1/messages') stays under a small ceiling — so the guard's deletion reddens the suite. Generalize the row generator so any future defensive early-return in the read path is required to name the fixture that makes it fire.

summary: requireHttpUrl accepts a site_url carrying URL userinfo, and the plaintext-credential SECURITY warning then prints the whole site_url verbatim — so a password embedded in site_url is written to stderr. The package's secret-hygiene discipline keys on the config key NAME ('key|secret|token|password|credential'), so `site_url` is classified non-secret and this shape escapes it entirely.
failure: `connect({ site_url: 'http://bot:sup3rs3cret@zulip.example.com', email:'b@x', api_key:'realkey' })` → console.warn emits `[parley-zulip] SECURITY: site_url http://bot:sup3rs3cret@zulip.example.com is plaintext http:// ...`. cli.ts sends stderr to the operator's logs, and core surfaces connect diagnostics into model context. net-util's own credentialParts() redacts exactly this shape from thrown messages; this console.warn path bypasses it.
remediation: Either reject a site_url carrying username/password at connect() naming the key (it is redundant with the Basic header the plugin builds itself, and is the fail-fast answer), or strip userinfo when normalizing baseUrl in requireHttpUrl and warn on the stripped origin only.
testUpgrade: Extend the secret-hygiene table from key-NAME classification to VALUE classification: for every declared backend_config key, feed a value carrying a sentinel secret in each place a secret can hide (URL userinfo `http://u:SENTINEL@host`, a query value `?token=SENTINEL`, a path segment `/bot:SENTINEL/`), and assert the sentinel appears in no console.warn/console.error/thrown message/stack from connect() — accepted or rejected. The current SECRET_KEY regex over key names cannot see a credential smuggled into a non-secret-named key.

summary: `fetchRecent`'s `blockMs` budget is enforced per REST PAGE, not per CALL. `fetchWithin` computes `budget = deadline - Date.now()` once and hands that same DURATION to `fetchSince`, which passes it unchanged as `deadlineMs` to every page in its `while (messages.length < limit)` loop. net-util's `deadlineMs` is a per-call wall-clock duration (bridge-net-util/src/index.ts:400, `budget = deadlineMs - (now() - started)` with `started` local to that call), so each page restarts the clock. A call with `limit > 100` may therefore run up to `ceil(limit/100) x blockMs`. The `since === undefined` branch is worse: it passes no `deadlineMs` at all, so every page falls back to net-util's 30 s default regardless of `blockMs`. This is the exact class test/blocking-budget.test.ts declares in its header ('a call that overruns its own declared budget on a leg nobody bounded'), but every cell there uses the default limit of 100, i.e. exactly one page, so the paging loop is invisible to it.
failure: Reproduced against test/fake-discord.ts: channel provisioned, three 200-responses of 100 messages each injected with `delayMs: 900`, then `plugin.fetchRecent({ topic, since: asCursor('1'), limit: 300, blockMs: 1500 })` -> settles at 2745 ms against a 1500 ms budget. The same call with `since` omitted -> 2734 ms. Reachable from production: `parley_fetch_recent` accepts a model-supplied `limit` clamped to MAX_FETCH_LIMIT = 1000 (bridge-core/src/transport/tools.ts:42) and `block_ms` clamped to `catchup.block_max_ms` (60 s default), and `fetchRecentBlocking` spreads `...args` so `limit` reaches the plugin unchanged - so one tool call can occupy 10 x 60 s = 600 s while core sized the wait at 60 s for the client's tool timeout. MAX_FETCH_LIMIT's own stated purpose (bounding a DoS knob) is defeated by the same path.
remediation: Make the deadline ABSOLUTE rather than a duration inside the paging loop: thread `deadline` (epoch ms) down to `fetchSince`/`getMessages` and recompute `deadlineMs = deadline - Date.now()` per page, breaking out of the loop (returning the pages gathered so far with their real `nextCursor`) once it is <= 0. Give the `since === undefined` branch the same treatment so a no-`since` blocking call is bounded at all; where no `blockMs` was given, bound the whole multi-page walk by one shared budget instead of N x net-util's 30 s default.
testUpgrade: Widen test/blocking-budget.test.ts's CELLS table with a `limit` axis crossed against the existing STALLS: `LIMITS = [1, PAGE_LIMIT, PAGE_LIMIT + 1, 3 * PAGE_LIMIT, 1000]`, each row seeding or injecting enough full pages to force `ceil(limit/100)` round trips with a per-page delay strictly BELOW the budget, and asserting the same `<= BLOCK_MS + SLACK_MS` invariant. Add a `since: undefined` row so the no-`since` branch joins the table. This guards the class 'a bound expressed as a per-attempt duration inside a loop that repeats the attempt' rather than the one 300-message instance; the existing cells are all single-page and can never see it.

summary: 11 of the 18 cases in long-poll.test.ts cannot fail on the plugin's native long-poll at all: both large tables drive core's `fetchRecentBlocking` (generic 250 ms poll wrapper), so core's fallback satisfies every assertion whether or not the plugin ever arms a waiter. The first table's comment concedes this; the SECOND table ('when the live transport dies mid-wait', 6 cells) explicitly claims the opposite - 'nothing else can wake that waiter: the message is durable over a healthy REST API while the call sleeps its whole budget' - and that claim is false, because it too runs through `fetchRecentBlocking` with `pollIntervalMs: 250`. A false rationale is worse than a missing one: it reads as coverage of waiter-death-mid-wait that nobody actually has.
failure: Mutation: `const socketLive = this.gatewayLive();` -> `const socketLive = false;` at src/index.ts:396, which disables the native long-poll entirely (no waiter is ever armed; `fetchRecent` degenerates to an immediate REST page). `npx vitest run packages/bridge-discord/test/long-poll.test.ts` -> 13 passed, 5 failed. All 5 transport-state cells and all 6 'dies mid-wait' cells stayed GREEN; only the 'a wakeup arriving' phases and the two disconnect cells caught it. Those 11 green cells each also step up to BLOCK_MS = 60 s of fake-timer time in 10-100 ms increments, so they cost wall-clock too.
remediation: Drive the mid-wait table through `plugin.fetchRecent(...)` directly (as the 'a wakeup arriving' describe already does), so the plugin's own waiter is the only thing that can return the message. If the wrapper is kept deliberately, rewrite the header comment to state what the cells actually assert (that the plugin composes with core's fallback without hanging or erroring in each transport state) and merge the two tables into one parameterized transport-state x loss-time table, since they then assert the same property.
testUpgrade: Add a caller axis to the file so every future long-poll cell declares which layer it can discriminate: `CALLERS = [['plugin (native)', (p, args) => p.fetchRecent({...args, blockMs})], ['core wrapper', (p, args) => fetchRecentBlocking(p, args, {blockMs, pollIntervalMs: 250})]]` crossed with the existing transport/loss rows, plus a negative control that runs the native rows with the waiter suppressed and asserts they FAIL. This guards the class 'a plugin-level table whose assertions are satisfied by a core-level fallback', which recurs on every backend that has both a native and a wrapped blocking path.

summary: Whether an absent Discord channel is reported as `NoSuchTopicError` or as a plain empty page depends on how much of `blockMs` is left when the REST 404 lands. `fetchWithin` returns `{ messages: [], nextCursor: since }` when `budget <= 0`, and its catch swallows ANY error - `NoSuchTopicError` included - once `Date.now() >= deadline`. With a small `block_ms` the gateway-connect leg (`withDeadline(this.ensureGateway(), blockMs)`) or a slow query eats the budget, so the absent-topic signal is silently replaced by an ordinary empty window and core never sets `topicAbsent: true`. Both answers are individually legal per the seam, but the same input flipping between them on a timing race reproduces exactly the 'idle bridge with no error' failure the rest of this package works hard to avoid.
failure: Reproduced against test/fake-discord.ts with a channel id that was never created: `plugin.fetchRecent({ topic: asTopic('7999999'), since: asCursor('1'), blockMs })` gives `blockMs: 1 -> {messages:[],nextCursor:"1"}`, `blockMs: 5 -> {messages:[],nextCursor:"1"}`, `blockMs: 20 -> NoSuchTopicError`. `block_ms` is clamped from above by `catchup.block_max_ms` but never floored, so a model may pass `block_ms: 1`. Operator consequence: a mistyped channel id in parley.config.yaml reports an empty window forever instead of 'topic not present yet'.
remediation: Classify absence before the budget can erase it: let `NoSuchTopicError` escape `fetchWithin`'s post-deadline catch unconditionally (it is a classification, not a transport failure), and issue the first exclusive-`since` query before spending budget on `ensureGateway`, or reserve a minimum slice of `blockMs` for it. A zero or negative budget should still make the one query it owes rather than answering from nothing.
testUpgrade: Parameterize the existing 'a topic with no backend representation' READS table in test/rest-contract.test.ts over a BUDGETS axis - `[0, 1, 5, 50, BLOCK_MS]` - crossed with an injected query latency above and below that budget, asserting the SAME classification (`NoSuchTopicError`) in every cell. The current table pins only `BLOCK_MS = 2000`, the one column that cannot see the flip. The class is 'a seam classification decided after a budget check', so the widened table should cover every seam-level error the blocking path can swallow, not just absence.

summary: Once the Socket Mode handshake succeeds, blockForMessage breaks out of the degradation ladder and performs zero further conversations.history reads for the rest of the budget, so a stream that establishes but never delivers withholds already-durable history for the whole block_ms.
failure: connect({app_token}) on a workspace whose Event Subscriptions lack `message.channels` (or whose app_token is shared with another process, so events land on the other connection). fetchRecent({topic, since:'0', blockMs:4000}); a message becomes durable in conversations.history at t=400ms. Observed: returns at t=4036ms with only 3 history reads. Same shape with an established socket dropped 300ms into the park and dials failing: durable at t=700ms, returned at t=4008ms. At the default catchup.block_max_ms of 60s this is a full minute of silent delay per message, which is exactly the harm the README's ladder paragraph claims to have removed.
remediation: Do not treat a successful handshake as proof the stream serves. Keep the rung loop running when `live` is true — arm the waiter for min(remaining, rungMs) unconditionally and re-query each rung (a slower live-mode cadence, e.g. MAX_DIAL_BACKOFF_MS, keeps the healthy-socket cost at ~block_ms/5000 reads) — and additionally drain the channel's waiters whenever the shared socket closes or `wsReady` is reset, so a mid-park drop falls back to the ladder instead of parking to the deadline.
testUpgrade: Widen the DEGRADATIONS table in test/blocking-fetch.test.ts, whose every row today makes the handshake FAIL before the call starts, with a 'handshake succeeds, stream does not serve' axis: (a) fake greets but never pushes an events_api envelope, (b) socket established then dropped mid-park with apps.connections.open failing, (c) socket established, dropped, and recovered mid-budget. Cross each with the existing LANDING_FRACTIONS and grade against the same dueBy() ladder plus the existing per-method ceilings, so the class is pinned by delivery latency rather than by which way the handshake failed.

summary: FakeSlack.history ignores body.limit entirely, so the page size the plugin actually asks Slack for is unpinned; the README cost model is 'verified' against the HISTORY_PAGE_LIMIT constant rather than against anything on the wire.
failure: Mutating runFetch's request body from `{ channel, limit: HISTORY_PAGE_LIMIT }` to `{ channel }` leaves the whole package suite green: 430/430 passed. Against real Slack that mutation halves the page to the API default of 100, doubling the request count of the documented `backlog^2 / (2 * limit * page)` model — while documented-scopes.test.ts still passes because it only checks the README string `page = 200` against the constant, a number no request now carries.
remediation: Make the fake serve `min(body.limit ?? 100, pageSize)` objects per page (real Slack semantics: it serves at most what you asked and may serve fewer), and record the requested limit so a test can assert it reached the wire.
testUpgrade: Add a parameterized 'the wire carries what the source asks for' case over the request-shaping constants: for each of pageSize in {15, 50, 1000} assert the observed page length equals min(HISTORY_PAGE_LIMIT, pageSize) and that the recorded `limit` form field equals HISTORY_PAGE_LIMIT — so dropping, renaming or retyping any history request parameter changes an observable page count instead of nothing. Generalise the same shape to `oldest`/`cursor`, which today are only pinned by one bespoke http-contract case.

summary: emptyCursor throws away newestSeenTs on the no-`since` path even when the walk ran to exhaustion, returning the '0' sentinel; the `since` path already returns newestSeenTs from the identical information.
failure: Channel seeded with 300 `channel_join` records and no surfacable message. fetchRecent({topic, limit:100}) walks all 6 pages, returns messages:[] and nextCursor '0'. Core persists '0' via readState.set, so the next catch-up re-walks the entire channel (6 pages again) before it can advance. Worse, on a channel whose full history exceeds MAX_HISTORY_PAGES with fewer than `limit` surfaced messages (400k entries at a full page, ~30k on the reduced 15-object tier the README documents), the no-`since` call throws `exceeded 2000 pages` and, having no stored cursor to resume from, throws on every subsequent catch-up with no in-band recovery — the README's 'reset that topic's cursor' remedy presumes a cursor exists.
remediation: In emptyCursor, return newestSeenTs whenever the walk ran to exhaustion (`pageCursor === undefined` on exit), for the no-`since` path as well as the `since` path; keep `args.since ?? asCursor('0')` only for a walk that stopped early. The safety argument in the existing JSDoc — every entry above the floor was seen and none was surfacable — applies identically.
testUpgrade: In test/catchup-window.test.ts drop the `if (sinceMode !== 'none')` guard so the final-cursor assertion runs for every since mode, and add an 'all-unsurfaced' layout row asserting (a) the first no-`since` page's nextCursor is the newest raw entry's ts and (b) the second drain iteration costs O(1) pages — a request-count assertion, so a cursor that merely 'looks' advanced but re-walks still fails.

summary: subscribe calls ensureSocket directly, bypassing the clear missing-app_token guard that ensurePollSocket owns, so a reactive-only deployment gets an opaque vendor error and one futile dial per topic against Slack's tightest-limit endpoint.
failure: connect({api_url, bot_token}) with no app_token, then subscribe(asTopic('C0NOAPP'), handler) rejects with `SlackApiError: Slack apps.connections.open -> not_authed` and fake.hits('apps.connections.open') === 1. With five configured topics that is five token-less dials at startup and five occurrences of an error message that names neither app_token nor Socket Mode, while ensurePollSocket already has the exact sentence an operator needs ('Slack Socket Mode needs an app_token; this deployment has no live push').
remediation: Hoist the `this.appToken === undefined` rejection into ensureSocket (or check it at the top of subscribe) so both entry points fail with the same named error and neither dials.
testUpgrade: Parameterize a table over the entry points that need the shared socket (`subscribe`, blocking `fetchRecent`) crossed with (`app_token absent`, `app_token present`): the absent rows must reject/degrade with a message matching /app_token/ AND leave fake.hits('apps.connections.open') === 0. Today only the blocking-fetch/absent cell is covered, by one assertion inside the DEGRADATIONS table.

summary: The docblock says subscribe's reachability probe catches 'a missing `message.channels` event subscription'; the probe is a conversations.history read, which succeeds in exactly that configuration.
failure: Provision the app with the bot invited to a channel and `channels:history` granted but no `message.channels` event subscription. subscribe() resolves: apps.connections.open succeeds, hello arrives, and the limit:1 history probe returns ok:true. No message event is ever pushed, so the topic delivers nothing forever — precisely the outcome the docblock says cannot happen, and the configuration that makes finding #1 cost 60s per message.
remediation: Correct the docblock to the two absences the probe genuinely detects (a typo'd channel_map target and a channel the bot was never invited to), matching the accurate comment already on subscribe in src/index.ts, and cross-reference the live-source-not-serving behaviour instead of implying it is guarded.
testUpgrade: Extend the absent-topic CODES table with a `deliverability` axis alongside `absentFor`, carrying an explicit row for 'history readable but no events subscribed' whose stated expectation is 'subscribe resolves and delivers nothing' — so the gap is a declared, reviewable decision rather than a prose claim no case grades.

summary: The rate-limit paragraph claims an unavailable Socket Mode costs 'O(log block_ms) reads and dials per blocked call', but the ladder caps at MAX_DIAL_BACKOFF_MS, making the rung count linear in block_ms once past the cap.
failure: Applying the plugin's own rungStarts recurrence: block_ms=60000 gives 16 rungs (coincidentally near log2), but catchup.block_max_ms is operator-configurable — block_ms=600000 gives 124 rungs against log2(600000) ~= 20. An operator who raises block_max_ms to ten minutes on the strength of an O(log) claim gets ~124 conversations.history reads and ~124 apps.connections.open dials per blocked fetch_recent on one channel, which on the README's own reduced tier (one request per minute) is two orders of magnitude over budget.
remediation: State the bound the code actually implements: roughly 4 + block_ms/MAX_DIAL_BACKOFF_MS reads and dials per blocked call (about 16 at the default 60s), and note that it grows linearly if block_max_ms is raised.
testUpgrade: Extend the documented-scopes rate-limit paragraph checks — which already pin DIAL_BACKOFF_MS and MAX_DIAL_BACKOFF_MS by value — with a case that computes rungStarts(blockMs).length for a table of blockMs values {4000, 60000, 600000} and asserts the README states a bound consistent with it, so any future re-shaping of the ladder must move the prose.

summary: Six near-identical 'start a fake, connect a plugin, tear both down' helpers are restated across the suite instead of shared, so a fixture change has to be made six times and a divergence between them is invisible.
failure: `withPlugin` appears in vendor-markup.test.ts:48 and mention-markup.test.ts:210 differing only in mention_map and handshake_timeout_ms; `harness()` in envelope-robustness.test.ts:108; `makePlugin` + `capture` + `settleWithin` in connection-lifecycle.test.ts:39; `deliver` in blocking-fetch.test.ts:42; `makeContext` in conformance.test.ts:11; plus `listen`/`stop`/`readBody` in http-contract.test.ts. When the constructor gained handshake_timeout_ms only two of the six adopted it, so the classification and markup suites silently run on the 10s default while the lifecycle suite runs on 400ms — a divergence no test can report.

summary: `post` resolves with a `backendMsgId` even when `ingest`/`store.append` recorded nothing, so an accepted message is invisible to `fetchRecent` forever and the only signal is one stderr line a minute.
failure: Reproduced (test/aprobe.test.ts probe F, since deleted): with `ObservedStore.isOpen()` false and `append()` returning undefined — what `compactIfDue`'s `finally { this.fd = openSync(...) }` leaves behind when the reopen fails with EMFILE/EACCES/ENOENT — three `post()` calls all resolve ('-1009111222:1..3'), all three texts reach the fake upstream, `fetchRecent` then returns `[]` with nextCursor '0' (a REGRESSED cursor), and stderr carries exactly ONE 'dropped a message' line for the three losses because `report` throttles the class to 60s. The same store state silently discards every inbound getUpdates message after the update has already been acknowledged to Telegram, and nothing ever retries the open, so the bridge is a permanent black hole that reports healthy. The plugin already treats this exact outcome as unacceptable on the teardown path (index.ts:285-291 throws an error naming the id and the store path) — the store-refusal cause is simply unguarded.
remediation: Make `ingest` report refusal to its caller (return the record or a reason) and have `post` throw the same 'accepted upstream, missing locally' error naming `<chat>:<mid>` and `storePath` when nothing was stored. Separately, treat `!store.isOpen()` as a connection fault: attempt a reopen, and fail seam calls rather than accepting writes into a store that cannot hold them.
testUpgrade: Parameterize a table over CAUSE-of-refusal x seam-call: {no append descriptor, chat cap refuses, append throws} x {post, inbound getUpdates ingest}, asserting for every cell that either (a) the record is retrievable via fetchRecent, or (b) the call rejects with a message naming the id and the store path — never 'resolved and missing'. The existing TEARDOWN_CELLS table in protocol.test.ts covers only the disconnect cause and should be widened to this axis; protocol.test.ts's 'names $name as the reason a record was dropped' asserts the stderr text only and passes while post lies.

summary: `append()` runs `compactIfDue()` AFTER the record is durably written and indexed, so a compaction failure throws out of a successful write — the caller skips `wakeWaiters` and every live subscriber, and the loop misreports the message as dropped.
failure: Reproduced (probe A): with `observed_retention_per_chat: 1` and one forced ENOSPC inside `compactIfDue`, an injected message 'two' ends up STORED (fetchRecent returns ['two']) but is NEVER delivered to the live subscriber (live === ['one']), while stderr says `dropped update 2: ENOSPC`. The same throw skips `wakeWaiters`, so a `fetchRecent({since, blockMs: 60000})` parked on that chat hangs for the full budget despite the message it is waiting for being in the store. store-compaction.test.ts already pins that the record survives ('m51' on disk and in entries) — it just never looks at the plugin-level consequence.
remediation: Compaction is an amortization concern, not a durability one: catch inside `compactIfDue` (or after it in `append`) and report, so `append` returns the stored record whenever the record was written. Never let a post-write step convert a success into an exception.
testUpgrade: A parameterized case over FAILING-STEP within append {appendFileSync, index, applyRetention, compactIfDue} asserting the invariant 'a record visible to fetchRecent was also pushed to every live subscriber and woke every parked waiter, or the record is absent everywhere' — i.e. store-visibility and delivery never disagree. inbound.test.ts's 'keeps consuming updates when store append throws' only fails the write itself, which is the one step where the two agree.

summary: Compaction opens the predictable path `<store_path>.tmp` with 'w' (no O_EXCL, symlinks followed) and then renames it over the store, so anyone who can create a file in the store's directory redirects the full plaintext of every observed message.
failure: Reproduced (probe E): pre-planting `store.jsonl.tmp` as a symlink to `victim.txt` and driving 8 appends under `maxPerChat: 2` overwrites victim.txt with `#evicted ["-1:1","-1:2"]` plus the message records ('secret-3' …). `restrictMode(tmp)` also chmods the link target. Reachable whenever `store_path` is placed in a shared directory (e.g. /tmp) or the state dir pre-exists with loose modes — `mkdirSync(..., {mode: 0o700})` only applies to directories the store itself creates. store.test.ts's permissions table deliberately exercises a leftover `.tmp` and asserts it is REUSED, so the current suite endorses the behaviour.
remediation: Create the temp file with `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` (`openSync(tmp, 'wx')` plus a retry on a unique suffix), or use a randomized name in the store's own directory; refuse to compact through an existing non-regular file.
testUpgrade: A parameterized security case over PRE-EXISTING-TMP kind {regular world-readable file, symlink to a file outside the store dir, symlink to a directory, FIFO} asserting the compaction either fails loudly or writes only to a fresh regular file inside the store directory — and that no path outside `store_path` is modified. This also guards the analogous hazard on the store file itself.

summary: All three 'don't poison the memo on transient failure' recovery paths (chatIdByTopic, canonicalById, getMe) are vacuously covered — deleting them leaves the whole package suite green, while the behaviour they prevent is a permanently unusable topic.
failure: Mutation: replacing the three `.delete(...)` lines (index.ts:453, :500, :651) with no-ops keeps `npx vitest run packages/bridge-telegram` at 327 passed / 3 skipped. The difference is user-visible: with `failMethod('getChat', {status: 500, times: 1})`, the unmutated plugin answers the FIRST `fetchRecent({topic: '@mychannel'})` with an error and the SECOND with 'ok'; the mutant rejects every later call for the life of the connection, so one transient 500 makes the topic permanently unresolvable (posts, subscribes and catch-up all fail, and core's presence loop swallows the rejection).
remediation: Keep the code; add coverage. Also consider bounding what is memoized negatively at all, so the rule is structural rather than three hand-copied catch blocks.
testUpgrade: A parameterized table over MEMO {getMe, getChat/@name resolution, topic→chat resolution} x FAILURE {500 once, transport error once, 429-then-ok} x CALL {post, fetchRecent, subscribe, resolveIdentity}, asserting the first call rejects and the next identical call succeeds against the same instance. docs.test.ts's 'is offline-safe' case is the near-miss: it makes getChat fail permanently and only ever calls once.

summary: `call()` returns `res.json()` with no check of Telegram's `ok`/`result` envelope, so a 2xx `{"ok":false}` passes `connect`'s advertised fail-fast preflight and resurfaces later as a contextless TypeError.
failure: Reproduced (probe B): stubbing `/getMe` to answer HTTP 200 `{"ok":false,"error_code":400,"description":"nope"}` makes `connect()` RESOLVE — README line 21 claims connect 'Verifies the token with getMe (fails fast … rather than coming up as a silent black hole)' — and `resolveIdentity` then rejects with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'username')`, naming neither the call nor the upstream. The same shape on `/sendMessage` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'chat')` after Telegram has accepted the message, and on `/getChat` reports the topic as unresolvable with the same opaque text. Reachable via a middlebox/captive portal or a local Bot API server (`api_url` is a documented knob).
remediation: Add one envelope check in `call()`: reject with `<label> → ok:false: <description>` when `ok !== true`, and when the expected `result` is absent — the same place Slack's `ok:false` is interpreted per net-util's own note that response shapes belong in the caller.
testUpgrade: A parameterized table over MALFORMED-2xx {ok:false with description, ok:true with no result, result of the wrong type, empty body} x ENDPOINT {getMe, getChat, sendMessage, getUpdates}, asserting connect rejects (preflight endpoints) or the seam call rejects with an error naming the endpoint and the upstream description — never a TypeError.

summary: net-util bounds, flattens and redacts every untrusted body before it can become an Error, but the plugin's success path calls `res.json()` directly, so a hostile 2xx body reaches the MCP error result raw.
failure:
Reproduced (probe C): a 200 response whose body is `HOSTILE-PAYLOAD-…` makes `post` reject with `Unexpected token 'H', "HOSTILE-PA"... is not valid JSON` — upstream bytes verbatim. Node embeds the snippet unescaped: `JSON.parse("

HELLO")` yields `Unexpected token 'H', "

HELLO" is not valid JSON` and a leading U+202E is carried through as-is, which is exactly the forged line structure and bidi override `sanitizeBody`'s NEUTRALIZED class exists to strip before a thrown message becomes an `isError` tool result.
remediation: Parse the buffered text yourself and wrap the failure: `sanitizeBody(text)` (via net-util) in a `<label> → body: …` error, instead of letting a raw `JSON.parse` SyntaxError escape.
testUpgrade: A parameterized case over HOSTILE-2xx-BODY {leading newlines, U+202E, U+0085/U+009B, a lone surrogate, 10MB of text} asserting the rejection message contains no raw control/format character and is bounded — run against every plugin that hands a body to `res.json()`, since this is a cross-backend class net-util already owns for the non-2xx path.

summary: Two `ObservedStore` branches are unreachable — the out-of-order binary-search insert and the seq-less legacy record path — and the comment defending the first describes a situation that cannot occur.
failure: Mutation: replacing the binary-search body (store.ts:459) and the `: this.nextSeq` fallback in `stamp()` (store.ts:436) with `throw new Error('MUTANT: …')` leaves the whole package suite green (327 passed / 3 skipped). Neither branch executes: `append` stamps strictly increasing seqs, and the on-disk file is written in global append order, so lines for one chat are already ascending — the comment's justification ('store lines interleaved across chats on reload') produces interleaving ACROSS chats, never out-of-order WITHIN one. The `stamp` fallback serves a seq-less record format this package has never published.
remediation: Delete both branches (push-at-tail; treat a record with no valid `seq` as a garbled line and drop it, which the surrounding try/catch already does) and delete the comments with them. If either is genuinely wanted, it needs a test that reaches it.
testUpgrade: Rather than a test per branch, add a package-level guard for the CLASS: assert store invariants over a generated append/reload sequence (random chats, random message_ids, reload at random points) and separately run the suite with these branches mutated to throw as part of the mutation budget — an unreachable branch is a finding, not coverage.

summary: The conformance context sets `concurrentPost: 'unsupported'` and is immediately followed by a comment reading 'NO concurrentPost, deliberately', and the file's opening comment describes chat-id shapes while sitting above `let seq = 0`.

testUpgrade: Not a runtime class — but the existing docs.test.ts hygiene lints (title uniqueness, rig duplication) can be extended with a check that every conformance context field a backend sets is either used or named in the same expression, so a stale narration about a field cannot survive the field changing.

summary: `credentialParts` keeps the pathname and its segments ONLY when they contain a `:`, so a token carried in an ordinary path segment (the `/api/webhooks/<id>/<token>` shape) is redacted only by the byte-exact URL split and the `scheme://` sweep. A body or transport that echoes the bare path leaks it into an MCP `isError` result.
failure: url = `https://api.example.test/api/webhooks/12345/SECRET-CANARY-9f3a`, upstream returns 404 with body `no route for /api/webhooks/12345/SECRET-CANARY-9f3a`. Reproduced: thrown message is `L → 404: no route for /api/webhooks/12345/SECRET-CANARY-9f3a` — the canary reaches model context and stderr. The existing SPELLINGS row 'the credential path alone, no scheme or host' passes only because its fixture URL is the Telegram `bot123:<token>` shape, which happens to contain a colon.
remediation: Drop the `includes(':')` filter: put the whole `pathname` and every path segment into `credentialParts` unconditionally, gated on a length threshold (e.g. `> 8`) rather than on punctuation, so an opaque token in any segment is covered. Then correct the README sentence, which today reads as if the path itself were always covered.
testUpgrade: Parameterize the CREDENTIAL_LOCATIONS table by credential SHAPE as well as location: add rows for a colon-less opaque path segment (`/api/webhooks/<id>/<token>`), a base64url token segment, and a token in a path segment with a `-`/`_` — crossed with the existing SPELLINGS × VECTORS grid. Better still, generate the URL from a `{location, shape}` product and assert the canary never appears, so the next credential shape is a row rather than a rewrite.

summary: The negative control's one-to-one-ness is enforced per CLAUSE, not per ASSERTION. Individual assertions inside a graded case can be deleted with the entire conformance package — reference suite, suite-shape, CLAUSES registry and the child broken-variant run — staying green, while eleven backends keep being certified against the gutted suite.
failure: Mutated packages/conformance/src/index.ts to neuter six assertions at once: the `Date.parse(m.timestamp)` validity check, `typeof/length` on `m.backendMsgId`, `typeof/length` on `m.cursor`, the SECOND `await ctx.plugin.disconnect()` (i.e. the entire 'idempotent' half of the 'disconnect is idempotent' clause), `typeof/length` on `id.backendRef`, and `expect(new Set(ids).size).toBe(3)` (post-returned ids unique). `npx vitest run packages/conformance` → 279/279 passed, 7/7 files. No BROKEN_VARIANT produces a bad timestamp, an empty cursor/backendMsgId/backendRef, a non-idempotent disconnect, or duplicate post-return ids.
remediation: Extend the mechanical control from clauses to the assertions a clause is built on. Add BROKEN_VARIANTS for the uncontrolled shapes (garbage `timestamp`; empty `cursor`; empty `backendMsgId`; a `disconnect` that throws on the second call; an empty `backendRef`; a `post` that returns a constant id while `fetchRecent` reports distinct ones) and record which case each must break, exactly as `mustFail` already does.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS by deriving the requirement from the suite source: parse `src/index.ts` for every `expect(` inside `expectWellFormedMessage` and each case, and require a mapping entry to a BROKEN_VARIANT for each — or, cheaper and durable, extend `BrokenVariant` with a `mutates` field naming the Message field / seam call it corrupts, and assert (from `CONTEXT_FIELDS` plus the `Message` keys) that every field the suite asserts on has at least one variant corrupting it. A table over `keyof Message` would have caught all four Message-field instances above at once.

summary: `oneRetryAfterValue` computes an HTTP-date `Retry-After` as `Date.parse(text) - Date.now()`, ignoring the response's own `Date` header. A client clock ahead of the server turns a real server-stated wait into a negative value, which `retryAfterFromHeader` filters out as 'no hint' — and the loop then retries at `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MS`, violating the module's central 'never retry sooner than the vendor asked' invariant.
failure: Reproduced. Server clock 60s behind the client; response carries `Date: <serverNow>` and `Retry-After: <serverNow+30s>`. `retryAfterFromHeader(res)` → `undefined`; `fetchWithRetry` then performs a single 500 ms wait and re-fires. The vendor asked for 30 000 ms; we retried 60× sooner — the exact escalation-into-a-ban path the file's own comments are written against. The mirror case (client clock behind) inflates a routine 2 s hint past `deadlineMs` and ends the call with `429: upstream asked for …ms, past this call's 30000ms deadline`.
remediation: When the value is an HTTP-date, compute the delta against the response's `Date` header if present and parseable (`Date.parse(retryAfter) - Date.parse(res.headers.get('date'))`), falling back to `Date.now()` only when no `Date` header is offered. That is what RFC 9110 §10.2.3 assumes and it makes the hint skew-invariant.
testUpgrade: Parameterize the existing `retryAfterFromHeader` HTTP-date rows over a clock-skew axis: `skewMs ∈ [-120_000, -1_000, 0, +1_000, +120_000]` × `[a date form hint, a delay-seconds hint]`, with the fixture setting a `Date` header at `now - skew`. Assert the computed hint is within a second of the server-intended duration for every skew, and that no performed wait in `fetchWithRetry` falls below it. The current `httpDate()` helper derives from the local clock, so no existing row can vary this axis.

summary: `await opts.retryAfterOf?.(res)` is not guarded. A caller-supplied parser that throws — the ordinary case of `res.clone().json()` on a Cloudflare/nginx HTML 429 page — propagates an arbitrary, unlabeled, unredacted error out of `fetchWithRetry`, defeating the `<label> → …` contract, the URL redaction, `sanitizeBody`, and `statusOf`.
failure: Reproduced: 429 with body `<html>rate limited</html>` and `retryAfterOf: async (r) => { await r.clone().json(); return 1; }`. `fetchWithRetry` rejects with a bare `SyntaxError` (`Unexpected token '<' …`). The message does not start with `L → `, `statusOf(err)` is `undefined` (so a caller branching on 429 sees nothing), and nothing has passed through `redactUrls`. The error-envelope suite's own describe is titled 'nothing leaves this module outside the label + redact + sanitize envelope' — this leaves it. All four shipped parsers happen to `try/catch` internally, so the escape is latent rather than currently firing.
remediation: Wrap the hook: `const parsed = usableHint(await Promise.resolve(opts.retryAfterOf?.(res)).catch(() => undefined));`. A parser that cannot read the body means 'no usable hint', not 'abort the call' — and fail-open here cannot retry sooner than the header floor, which is computed independently.
testUpgrade: Add a `retryAfterOf` row-shape axis to the PARSERS table used by the HEADER_ROWS × PARSERS grid: `['a throwing parser', () => { throw new SyntaxError('…') }]`, `['a rejecting parser', () => Promise.reject(new Error('x'))]`, `['a parser returning a non-number', () => 'soon' as never]`. Assert for every row that the rejection message starts with `${label} → ` and that `statusOf(err)` is 429 — which pins the envelope for every future hook shape, not just this one.

summary: The HEADER_ROWS × PARSERS grid asserts `expect(w).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(requestedMs)`, and eight of the 22 header rows ('zero', 'empty', 'unparseable', 'negative', 'absent', 'a date already past', 'a hexadecimal spelling', 'an exponent spelling') carry `requestedMs === 0`. Across six parsers that is 48 rows whose wait assertion is vacuously true, so the `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MS` floor — the module's only self-invented backoff, and a documented public claim — is asserted nowhere.
failure: Mutated `const wait = hinted ?? DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MS` to `const wait = hinted ?? Math.min(0, DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MS)` (token-preserving, so the source-text meta-check still passes): 320/320 tests green, with the loop now firing eight back-to-back requests at a hint-less 429 with zero delay. Separately mutating `usableHint`'s `ms > 0` to `ms >= 0` — which makes a `retryAfterOf` returning 0 count as a stated hint of 0 ms — also stayed 320/320 green, so the 'a zero parser' row grades nothing either.
remediation: Give each row a `minWaitMs` alongside `requestedMs`: `Math.max(requestedMs, DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MS)` for every 'retry' row, and assert `w >= minWaitMs`. Add one row pinning `waits` exactly `[DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MS]` for a bare 429 with no header and no parser.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS by refusing degenerate expectations in the generator itself: derive the expected wait from the row (`expected = usableHint(headerMs, parserMs) ?? DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MS`) rather than from the row's stated `requestedMs`, and assert `expect(expected).toBeGreaterThan(0)` before using it — so any future row whose expectation collapses to zero fails at construction instead of passing vacuously. The same shape applies to the `w >= 0` idiom anywhere it appears.

summary: `tsconfig.test.json` + the `typecheck:test` script exist in both packages and are asserted to be correctly aliased, but no automation ever runs them: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only `npm ci`, `npm run build` (`tsc -b`, whose per-package `include` is `src/**` only), the dev-infra script, `npm test` (vitest, which transpiles without typechecking) and `preflight:publish`. No fixture in the repo is ever seen by a compiler.
failure: Traced: `grep typecheck .github/workflows` returns nothing; every package `tsconfig.json` has `"include": ["src/**/*"]`. A type error introduced anywhere under `packages/conformance/test/` or `packages/bridge-net-util/test/` passes CI in full. This falsifies readme.test.ts's row 'is not vacuous: some package does typecheck its test sources' — that row measures the presence of a `test/` include glob, not the execution of any gate — and it undercuts repo-contract.test.ts's own stated rationale ('the one gate that would have caught a changed public surface').
remediation: Add a CI step that runs the test typechecks (e.g. `npm run typecheck:test --workspaces --if-present`, after `npm run build` since it needs each dependency's `dist/*.d.ts`). Note that without a prior build the conformance gate cannot even resolve `@sharptrick/parley-core`, so ordering is load-bearing.
testUpgrade: Make the property mechanical rather than declarative: in repo-contract.test.ts, read `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and assert that some step invokes each package's `typecheck:test` script (or `tsc -p …/tsconfig.test.json`), parameterized over the set of packages that ship a `tsconfig.test.json`. That is the same trick the file already uses for `paths`, applied to the half that decides whether the config is alive.

summary: Every `blockMs` call in the suite passes a `since` (lines 491, 500, 515, 542, 547, 555). `seam.ts` states 'Blocking only engages relative to a `since`; with no `since` the default recent window returns at once', and core's `fetchRecentBlocking` really does call `plugin.fetchRecent({ ...args, since: undefined, blockMs: remaining })` on its first iteration — so the since-less blocking path is on the hot path for every `parley_fetch_recent` with `block_ms` and no cursor, and no clause grades it.
failure: A plugin that parks for the full `blockMs` on `fetchRecent({ topic, blockMs: 30000 })` with no `since` and a non-empty topic — i.e. holds a caller who asked for the recent window for 30 s and then returns it — passes conformance in full. Nothing in CLAUSES names this behaviour and no BROKEN_VARIANT produces it. (Note also that seam.ts and engine/blocking-fetch.ts state opposite rules for the since-less case; the suite grades neither.)
remediation: Add a clause to CLAUSES and a case: post a message, then `fetchRecent({ topic, blockMs: 5000 })` with no `since` — assert it returns the window promptly (well under `blockMs`) on both `supportsBlockingFetch` arms — plus the empty-topic variant, asserting whichever rule the repo settles on. Reconcile seam.ts and blocking-fetch.ts first, since they currently disagree.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS by parameterizing the blocking clause over `since ∈ {undefined, tail}` × `topicState ∈ {empty, has-messages}` rather than adding one case: the table then also covers the since-less-empty combination and any future blocking rule change has a row waiting for it. Add the matching BROKEN_VARIANT ('a fetch that parks on a since-less blockMs') so the new assertions have a control, per the ratchet this package already applies at clause granularity.

summary: `it.each(cases().map(c => [c.title]))('makes every capability branch of %s assert')` registers one row per suite case (21), but its body only asserts inside `for (const {field, region} of guardedRegions(owner.body))`. Only four cases contain a `ctx.<capability>` guard with an `if (` header, so ~17 rows execute an empty loop and assert nothing at all while presenting as coverage in the run summary.
failure: Rows such as 'makes every capability branch of topics are isolated assert' and '… of post accepts inReplyTo and the reply is durable, in order assert' cannot fail for any mutation of the suite; they are indistinguishable in the report from the four rows that do work. A reader auditing 84 suite-shape tests cannot tell which ones grade anything.
remediation: Collapse to a single case that flat-maps every case's guarded regions into one list, asserts the list is non-empty (so the check itself is not vacuous), and then asserts each region contains `expect(`. That both removes the dead rows and adds the missing non-vacuity guard.
testUpgrade: Apply the pattern as a rule rather than a fix: build the table FROM the guarded regions (`cases().flatMap(c => guardedRegions(c.body).map(r => [c.title, r.field, r.region]))`) so a row exists exactly when there is something to grade, and add one row asserting the derived table's length is greater than three — which is what catches the detector regressing to seeing nothing. The same 'row per candidate rather than per finding' shape applies to the neighbouring `reads the required field` and `still grades the clause` tables.

summary: `NULL_BODY_STATUS` (204/205/304) is unreachable. Per the fetch spec a null-body status always yields `res.body === null`, which `readBounded` short-circuits at line 257 returning `text: ''`; `buffered` then already nulls the body via `text.length === 0`. Its comment ('the constructor throws if one is given') documents a hazard the code cannot reach.
failure: Mutated `const NULL_BODY_STATUS = new Set([204, 205, 304])` to `new Set<number>([])`: 320/320 net-util tests green. The `returns an allowStatuses status (204)` row constructs `new Response(null, {status: 204})`, so the `text.length === 0` arm claims it either way — the set has never been the thing under test.
remediation: Delete `NULL_BODY_STATUS` and its use, leaving `const body = text.length === 0 ? null : text;`. If it is kept as belt-and-braces, it needs a test that can distinguish it — and there is no way to construct one, which is the argument for deleting it.
testUpgrade: Rather than adding a test for unreachable code, guard the CLASS with mutation coverage on the module's constant tables: parameterize a meta-test over the module's small internal constant sets (`NULL_BODY_STATUS`, `DELAY_SECONDS`, `NEUTRALIZED`, `LONE_SURROGATE`) asserting each has at least one behavioural row that fails when the constant is emptied — run as a one-off mutation audit rather than in CI, and delete whatever cannot be distinguished.

summary: `listen()`'s double-start guard tests `httpServer?.listening`, which is false for the entire interval between `app.listen()` and the `listening` event — so two overlapping `listen()` calls both bind, and the comment's stated protection ("its presence loop beating past close()") does not hold.
failure: Traced, not reproduced. `listen(8080)` and `listen(8081)` issued without awaiting the first: both see `httpServer?.listening !== true`, both call `app.listen`, both call `announce()`. `httpServer` and `presence` are each overwritten by the second, so the first bound socket and its presence loop are orphaned — the first keeps heartbeating `hello`/`heartbeat` to the shared presence topic with no way to stop it, advertising a bridge nobody can reach, and `close()` can never close the first socket. The sequential case is safe (the first has fired `listening` before the second runs), which is why the existing test passes.
remediation: Latch a `starting` boolean synchronously at the top of the `listen` executor and reject the second call on it (clearing it on a bind failure), rather than inferring liveness from `server.listening`.
testUpgrade: Table the lifecycle-idempotence class across both roots: for each of {two overlapping `listen()`s, `listen()` racing `close()`, `close()` twice, `attach()` twice on the stdio bridge, `shutdown()` racing `attach()`}, assert exactly one live socket / one presence loop and that `close()`/`shutdown()` leaves zero beats after it returns. Every existing case awaits the first call, so none of them enters the race window.

summary: `onGroupchat` drops a live stanza with no `<body>` (`if (body === null) return;`), but `onMamResult` has no such filter — it stores `body: inner.getChildText('body') ?? ''`. Any archived stanza without a body (MUC subject change, XEP-0308 correction, XEP-0424 retraction, a chat-state or `<x/>`-only stanza) therefore becomes a `Message` with `content: ''` on catch-up that live push never emitted, contradicting the README's "identical via live push and via catch-up". The same items also hit `toMessage`'s `sender: ... : this.handle` fallback when `from` is the room's bare JID, which invents a sender from the SASL *username*.
failure: Not reachable on Prosody's `mod_muc_mam` (verified live: a `<subject>` change and an `<x/>`-only groupchat message from a second account produced no MAM item). On a server whose MUC archive stores subject changes or corrections — ejabberd's `mod_mam` and any deployment with `muc_log_all_rooms`-style settings — `fetchRecent` returns `{ content: '', senderHandle: 'parley' }` entries that occupy cursor positions and are pushed into agent context as blank messages.
remediation: Filter in `onMamResult` the same way the live path does: skip a forwarded `<message>` with no `<body>` child (distinguish absent from empty-string). Separately, drop the `this.handle` fallback in `toMessage` — a resource-less `from` is a room-level stanza, not this bridge's own handle.
testUpgrade: Guard the CLASS "the live path and the catch-up path apply different admission filters to the same backend event". Add a parameterized fixture table of archive items — body-only, subject-only, body+subject, `<x/>`-only, resource-less `from` — fed BOTH through `FakeXmpp.deliver` (live) and through a MAM query, asserting the two paths yield the identical set of `backendMsgId`s. This shape recurs on every backend that has separate push and history decoders.

summary: The README states that with multiple Socket Mode connections 'every open socket receives every subscribed event and filters locally', and rests its multi-session fallback advice on it; Slack is widely understood to deliver each event to only ONE of an app's open connections.
failure: Two Parley processes configured per the README's weaker option ('its own app, or at least its own bot user') share one app_token, so both hold a Socket Mode connection on the same app. If Slack routes each event to a single connection, each session receives a roughly random half of the live pushes — silent, per-session live-path loss that only a manual fetch_recent recovers, on the exact configuration the README blesses. The plugin's own zero-gap rotation design (open the replacement before draining the old socket on `reason: 'warning'`) only makes sense under single-connection routing, so the two claims sit uneasily together.
remediation: Verify the current Socket Mode multi-connection routing rule against Slack's live docs. If events are not fanned out, correct the sentence and strengthen the guidance to 'a distinct Slack APP (distinct app_token) per push-capable session — a distinct bot user within one app is not sufficient'.
testUpgrade: Encode the decided vendor semantics in FakeSlack rather than in prose: make it deliver each events_api envelope to exactly one connected socket (round-robin) and add a case with two plugin instances sharing an app token asserting the documented outcome. The row fails until doc and fixture agree, which is what stops the next reviewer meeting this claim again in a different costume.

summary: The `MIN_IDLE_POLL_MS` floor under the sole ingestion loop applies only when `updates.length === 0`, so an upstream that answers immediately with a non-empty batch it never retires spins the loop with no delay at all.
failure: An upstream (proxy cache, non-conforming local Bot API server) that ignores `offset` and re-serves the same batch leaves `offset = Math.max(offset, u.update_id + 1)` unchanged and `updates.length > 0`, so the `if (updates.length === 0)` throttle is skipped every iteration: the loop issues getUpdates as fast as the socket allows against the operator's bot token — the exact flood the comment above the floor says it prevents — while every record is silently deduped, so no message loss makes it visible. Not reproduced: the fake always honours `offset`, and its `ignoreLongPoll(true)` mode only produces the empty-answer shape the floor does cover.
remediation: Move the floor out of the empty-answer branch: bound the whole iteration (e.g. throttle whenever the poll returned in well under `poll_timeout_s` AND `offset` did not advance), so cadence is a property of the loop rather than of the answer's shape.
testUpgrade: Extend the fake with an 'ignores offset' mode and parameterize the existing 'stays below a handful of polls a second at poll_timeout_s %i' table over UPSTREAM-MISBEHAVIOUR {ignores timeout, ignores offset, answers with an already-consumed batch, answers with non-message updates only} — one row per way a poll can return without progress.
